Title: Bombay HC transfers Lawyers' Assault Complaint to Matunga Police, demands CCTV Footage
#### Supreme Court Judgments. #### High Court Judgments. # Bombay HC transfers Lawyers' Assault Complaint to Matunga Police, demands CCTV Footage. The Bombay High Court has made the decision to transfer the complaint filed by two lawyers who were allegedly assaulted at the Antop Hill police station premises in May to the Matunga police station. The court has directed the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) in the Matunga division to conduct a fair and unbiased investigation under the supervision of the Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Zone-4. The division bench of Justice Revati Mohite-Dere and Justice Gauri Godse issued this order in response to a plea by advocates Sadhana Omprakash Yadav and Harikesh Mishra, who accused senior inspector Nasir Kulkarni and other police personnel of inaction and refusal to register a case over the alleged attack and illegal detention on May 18. The lawyers sought the registration of an FIR against the police officials under various sections, including attempt to murder and assault with intent to outrage modesty. During the hearing, the bench expressed concern about the handling of the case by the Antop Hill police station and decided to transfer it to another police station for an impartial investigation. They summoned the Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) of the Antop Hill division and instructed that the case be transferred to ensure an unbiased examination. To safeguard potential evidence, the court directed the Antop Hill police station to retrieve and transfer the CCTV footage from all seven cameras at the station premises between May 18 at 2:30 pm and May 19 at 00:30 am. The footage will be handed over to the ACP of the Matunga Division for examination. The court cautioned against any tampering or deletion of the footage and emphasized the need for preservation. Advocate Uday Warunjikar, representing the lawyers, raised concerns about the possibility of footage manipulation and deletion. The court acknowledged this issue and emphasized the importance of preserving the evidence. The court's decision aims to ensure an impartial investigation into the alleged assault and illegal detention of the lawyers. LatestLaws.com presents: Lexidem Offline Internship Program, 2026. fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet:
Title: Youth alleges brutal police assault in Vadodara: Alleges assault over numberless bike, modified silencer; ACP claims officer’s collar was grabbed
# Youth alleges brutal police assault in Vadodara:Alleges assault over numberless bike, modified silencer; ACP claims officer’s collar was grabbed. An alleged case of police brutality has surfaced at Vadodara’s Sayajiganj Traffic Police Station. A 30-year-old man has accused traffic police personnel, including a senior officer, of beating and torturing him after he was stopped for riding a motorcycle without a number plate. **Three policemen were standing near Akota Bridge Shani Dev Temple.** Kaushalsinh Vijendrasinh Jat (age 30), residing in a society in Manjalpur area of Vadodara city, was passing by Dandia Bazaar crossroads on his Bullet this morning. Meanwhile, three police personnel on duty at the West Division Traffic Office located in Sayajiganj area were standing near Akota Bridge Shani Dev Temple. The youth's Bullet did not have a number plate and also had a modified silencer. Even though the youth was willing to pay the fine, the three policemen started bullying him and allegedly took his keys, as accused by the rider. The youth made a video as the police were bullying him. The youth said he started recording a video when the policemen continued to argue with him. He alleged that instead of issuing a challan, the policemen bullied him and later forced him into a police van. The youth claimed he was beaten inside the police van. The youth was severely beaten, leaving welts on his body. The youth was admitted to the hospital with more severe injuries. He said the youth was violating multiple traffic rules. The ACP said he reached the office and asked his guard to bring the youth for counselling. When the youth did not come and allegedly created trouble, police personnel were asked to bring him in. The ACP stated that during the discussion, the youth grabbed a policeman by the collar. He said the youth became more aggressive, after which he was brought to the Sayajiganj office. Later, the youth’s parents and brother also reached the station and argued with the police. ACP Vyas said the youth was later taken to hospital by his family. He added that the police would file a complaint against the youth and take action as per the law.

Title: Condemn Brutal Police Assault on AISA Delhi President Saiyed
Vol. 29  /  No. 14  **/**  **Condemn Brutal Police Assault on AISA Delhi Presid...**. #### Report. # Condemn Brutal Police Assault on AISA Delhi President Saiyed. AISA has strongly condemned the brutal assault on its Delhi State President Saiyed by the Delhi Police on March 30, calling it a shocking instance of state-sponsored repression on student activists. Saiyed, along with AISA leaders, had gone to Barakhamba Road Police Station regarding the detention of some students when SHO Mahavir Singh  assaulted him. In a statement, AISA said that the modus operandi of the Delhi Police stands exposed as a “terrifying, state-sanctioned machinery designed to hunt student activists.” The organisation pointed to a series of recent incidents, including rape threats to Delhi University activists at Maurice Nagar Police Station on March 13 and violent attacks on JNU students by plainclothes goons under police protection, as evidence of a growing pattern of repression. AISA stated that the Delhi Police is acting as a “private militia of the RSS-BJP” and said that such actions amount to an attack on democratic rights and dissent. It also held the ruling BJP responsible for giving the police a “free hand” to unleash violence. AISA has demanded the immediate suspension of SHO Mahavir Singh and strict action against all those involved in the assault. Title: MCC Gujarat demands FIR, suspension of cops for brutal assault on Muslim minor in Rajkot police station
### MCC Gujarat demands FIR, suspension of cops for brutal assault on Muslim minor in Rajkot police station. The Minority Coordination Committee (MCC), Gujarat, has written to the Director General of Police, Gandhinagar, demanding immediate registration of an FIR and suspension of police personnel accused of brutally assaulting a Muslim minor, Sikandar Kalawadiya, at the Gandhigram Police Station in Rajkot. The written statement submitted by the victim’s grandmother, Najuben, states that Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Radhika Bharai was present at the time of the assault and had instructed a police officer, Pradeep Dangar, to beat the boy, saying, “Our ACP Bharai has ordered that he must be beaten.” The officers are also accused of pulling the boy’s hair violently while other policemen recorded videos of the act. The MCC’s letter accuses the police of repeatedly violating human rights within police stations and disobeying Supreme Court guidelines, including the D.K. Basu directives on custodial conduct.
